nodes.label: ProjectBridge Architecture and Product Invariants
nodes.rationale: The MVP is a modular monolith: each Django domain app owns its business rules and writes, reads use selectors, and cross-app changes go through the owning service. Questionnaire schemas are deterministic and versioned; passport mapping is explicit and conflicts require executor review. Chat persistence and submission use REST, while authenticated project WebSockets deliver events and validate configured origins. Invitations require matching verified email; shared document archiving and deletion require both participants? consent.

nodes.label: Versioned Questionnaire Mapping with Human Conflict Resolution
nodes.rationale: Deterministic questions and preserving submitted answers require immutable product-authored schema versions and explicit mappings. When an answer conflicts with a nonempty passport value, retaining both until executor review prevents silent overwrites and preserves provenance. Superseding correction drafts preserve the original answers and schema version, at the cost of additional records and review work.
nodes.norm_label: versioned questionnaire mapping with human conflict resolution

nodes.label: D06: Restoration withdraws a one-party pending deletion request
nodes.rationale: A pending request records only one participant?s consent. Leaving it pending after restoration makes it unapprovable and prevents a new request, while silently retaining that consent after restore contradicts the restored active state.
nodes.norm_label: d06: restoration withdraws a one-party pending deletion request

nodes.label: D07: Validate project chat WebSocket origins
nodes.rationale: Without origin validation, a foreign site could attempt to use a participant?s browser session to subscribe to project events. FRONTEND_BASE_URL and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS provide the allowlist; the originless health probe remains outside the chat authentication stack.
nodes.norm_label: d07: validate project chat websocket origins
